memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: this is a refuse-or-minimum case.

Key facts: the coin is down 55% over 30 minutes and 75% from its high, with a 0.98 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation and a 42-SOL sell wall in the last 15 minutes against 45 SOL of buys. Net flow is only +3 SOL, so the recent return is a thin bounce, not a reversal. Pool depth of 53 SOL means a $20 round trip faces the high end of the 1.4-5.1% cost band, and a 30-second order delay on a coin moving this fast adds slippage risk on top.

Sizing if the desk overrides: $5 ticket, 20% stop, 15-minute hold. Given the sell pressure, I would not add size.

Refusal conditions: I refuse any size if the brief's bundle share (42%) is not explained as operator-backed, since bundling plus a launch bot and heavy early selling fits a dump pattern. I also refuse if sell-to-buy exceeds 1.0 in any recent window, or if the 15-minute net flow turns negative again. My recommendation is to skip.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying is narrow. The first two minutes after graduation show 702 buyers spending 343 SOL with a top-5 buyer share of only 8.3%, which argues against a single whale-driven launch. Top-3 holder concentration on the curve is 7.7%, and no airdrop dump was seen. The coin is alive, and the last 15 minutes show a positive 8.4% return with net buy flow of 3.19 SOL.

But the brief undercuts most of this. Price is down 74.6% from its 30-minute high and 54.7% over 30 minutes. A 42% bundle share and a 0.98 sell-to-buy ratio in the launch window suggest heavy bot activity and recycled volume rather than durable demand. Net flow over 15 minutes is only 3.19 SOL against 42 SOL of sales. Pool depth of 53 SOL is thin for a $20 ticket, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat into any small bounce.

I see no honest case strong enough to buy now. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a dead-cat bounce into distribution. The coin is down 74.6% from its 30-minute high and 54.7% over 30 minutes, and the last 15 minutes show sellers (142) nearly matching buyers (139) with sell SOL at 42.13 against 45.32 bought. Net flow is only +3.19 SOL, so the recent +8.4% bounce is thin and sell-driven. Early distribution is also visible: a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.98 in the first two minutes after graduation, with a launch bot present. A 42% bundle share means insiders or bundled wallets likely hold a large slice that can exit into any rally. At a $18.5k market cap and only 53 SOL of pool depth, a $20 ticket moves the price, and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost eats a small bounce. A skip is the right call.
